title: Building an Interactive Connections-Style Review Game for an OBGYN Resident Teaching Session
goal: Define and select an interactive review-game format with Claude, gather and submit topic reference materials, pilot and scale the Connections grid design, finalize grid category contents, attempt and troubleshoot an animated PowerPoint build, manually build Grid 1's click-trigger animations, and replicate animations across remaining grids and finish.

Step 1.step_name: Define and select an interactive review-game format
Step 1.step_action: Brainstorm review-session format options with Claude, rejecting an initial case-reveal proposal and converging on an NYT Connections-style grid plus a mini crossword recap.

nodes.label: Define review-session goals and constraints
nodes.detail: States the session's parameters - 50 minutes, ~16 mixed-PGY OBGYN residents, 8 resident-led topics, two teams - and asks Claude for an engaging format that avoids the fatigue of past Jeopardy/Kahoot sessions.

nodes.label: Propose initial review-game approach and clarify hosting needs
nodes.detail: Sketches an initial game-show-style approach to fit the constraints and asks a clarifying question about whether she will run the session live/improvised or with prebuilt content.

nodes.label: Review the response about initial review-game approach and hosting needs
Specify solo-host, prebuilt-slide requirement
nodes.detail: Clarifies that she alone will run the session and wants a fully prebuilt, slide-based presentation created well ahead of time rather than a live-improvised game.

nodes.label: Propose concrete case-reveal format
nodes.detail: Asks three clarifying questions before continue generating.

nodes.label: Answer three clarifying questions
Provide a proposed template/structure and ask two additional clarifying questions
nodes.detail: Provides a proposed session structure, timing, scoring, and slide template, then asks two additional clarifying questions about the case content before building it out.

nodes.label: Ask for a different Jeopardy-like game instead of the case-file reveal
nodes.detail: Provide a new prompt 'I don't like this case file reveal. I want it to be a game more like Jeopardy, but a different game' instead of answering the clarifying questions.

nodes.label: Suggest alternative game formats and ask a follow-up question
nodes.detail: Suggests several alternative host-run, slide-based game formats, including Pyramid/Password-style, Wheel of Categories, Survivor Board, and Family Feud-style games, and recommends a hybrid Survivor Board + Feud-style structure. After finishing the response, Claude asks a follow-up question about which direction the user wants to build out first based on these suggestions, which the user skips/dismisses.

nodes.label: Review the response about alternative game formats
Request a longer list of Jeopardy-like alternatives
nodes.detail: Prompt: 'Give a longer list of slide-based pre-built games similar to jeopardy.'

nodes.label: Present broader menu of slide-based grid games
nodes.detail: Offers a longer list of prebuilt, host-run, grid/board-based game formats (Survivor board, Battleship, Connect-4, Family Feud, NYT Connections-style grid, etc.) as Jeopardy alternatives.

nodes.label: Review the response about menu of slide-based grid games
Favor Connections-grid concept, explore NYT-style games
nodes.detail: Responds positively to the Connections-grid option and asks Claude to expand on other NYT-style games (Connections, Wordle, crossword) that could fit the review.

nodes.label: Map NYT-style game options to review goals
nodes.detail: Explains how each NYT-style format trains a different cognitive skill and recommends pairing Connections (active review) with a crossword recap (wrap-up).

nodes.label: Review the response about NYT-style game options
nodes.detail: Claude asks a follow-up question about 'Want me to build out this 4-part structure in detail next?', which the user skips/dismisses.

nodes.label: Finalize format: Connections grid plus crossword recap
nodes.detail: Confirms the chosen format - Connections grids for the bulk of the review plus a mini crossword recap - and announces she will now supply the 8 topics and references.

user_response.label: adopt
user_response.reasoning: a1 is the source because she asks Claude for an engaging, interactive review format that isn't Jeopardy or Kahoot. a15 is the target because, after the refinement through a2 to a14 (case-file reveal, longer game list, NYT-style options), it recommends pairing Connections with a crossword recap. She confirms exactly that pairing and moves on to supply the topics, and the rest of the session builds Connections grids. The label is adopt because she takes Claude's recommended format as given.

nodes.label: Confirm the selected game format and await topic materials
Locate topic list and reference materials
nodes.detail: Opens her residency didactic-schedule spreadsheet and CREOG reference guide to identify which resident presented each of the 8 topics and what reference each lecture is based on.

nodes.label: Ask whether Claude can access references pasted in this format
nodes.detail: For each topic in turn, opens the relevant PowerPoint/PDF/reference document (downloading attachments as needed) and pastes the topic name plus citation into the Claude chat.
nodes.softwares: Claude (web), Adobe Acrobat Reader, File Explorer

nodes.label: Confirm it can fetch or search the sources and ask for the remaining topics
nodes.detail: For each submitted topic, web-searches to pull authoritative guideline content (prioritizing ACOG Practice Bulletins/Committee Opinions per her instruction) and logs a content summary earmarked for the Connections grids.

nodes.label: Submit ERAS guidelines as the Topic 1 review
Search for and summarize Topic 1 ERAS guideline content
Locate thromboprophylaxis references
Submit Topic 2 thromboprophylaxis references to Claude
Search for Topic 2 authoritative ACOG guidance on thromboprophylaxis in pregnancy
Enter the next prompt and locate additional topic references in the CREOG guide
nodes.detail: Next prompt: 'Yes use the ACOG content primarily whenever possible'.
nodes.softwares: Claude, Microsoft Excel, Microsoft OneDrive, Adobe Acrobat Reader

nodes.label: Skip reading Topic 2 authoritative ACOG guidance on thromboprophylaxis
Confirm prioritization of ACOG guidelines for all topics
Submit patient positioning references for Topic 3
Retrieve Topic 3 ACOG guidance and summarize patient positioning considerations
Locate ACOG breast disorder guidelines and search for CREOG lecture materials
Submit benign breast disorder references for Topic 4 on benign breast disorders
Summarize Topic 4 benign breast disorder guidelines and identify Connections grid categories
Review the response about benign breast disorder guidelines and Connections grid categories
Locate BRCA Surveillance PDF
Send Topic 5 BRCA Surveillance
Summarize Topic 5 BRCA Surveillance
Locate pelvic organ prolapse references and review lecture slides
nodes.softwares: Adobe Acrobat Reader, Microsoft OneDrive, Microsoft PowerPoint

nodes.label: Submit pelvic organ prolapse repair materials for Topic 6
Summarize pelvic organ prolapse repair content for Connections and crossword games
Search the CREOG reference guide for Topic 7 laparoscopy references
Submit Topic 7 laparoscopy references (detail: laparoscopy only)
nodes.detail: Retrieves and submits the remaining topic reference material - laparoscopy troubleshooting and endometrial hyperplasia/PTEN - completing all 8 logged topics.

nodes.label: Summarize Topic 7 laparoscopy troubleshooting and identify Connections grid categories
Reopen and check the CREOG reference guide from Downloads
Review the response about laparoscopy troubleshooting and Connections grid categories
Locate and submit endometrial hyperplasia and PTEN references and send to Claude as Topic 8
nodes.detail: The participant finds the references for endometrial hyperplasia and PTEN immunoreactivity in the CREOG guide, then copies and pastes them into Claude as Topic 8.

nodes.label: Summarize Topic 8 endometrial hyperplasia and PTEN immunoreactivity findings
Review the response about endometrial hyperplasia and PTEN immunoreactivity findings
Request a single pilot grid before full build
nodes.detail: Asks Claude to build one example Connections grid first so she can confirm she likes the format before generating all 8. Prompt: 'Show me one grid as an example to make sure I like it first.'

nodes.label: Build pilot Connections grid and ask about difficulty
nodes.detail: Builds a pilot Connections grid from two paired topics (pelvic organ prolapse repair + laparoscopy) and presents two versions - a straightforward one and a trickier, cross-cutting one with tempting false pairings - asking which style she prefers.

nodes.label: Review the response about the pilot Connections grid, its four categories, and distractors
nodes.detail: Claude asks a follow-up question about difficult/trickiness level feels right, which the user skips/dismisses.

nodes.label: Regenerate the pilot Connections grid
nodes.detail: Regenerate the same prompt: 'Show me one grid as an example to make sure I like it first.'

nodes.label: Generate a revised pilot Connections grid with four categories and misleading pairings
Review the response about the regenerated pilot Connections grid and its misleading pairings
nodes.detail: Claude asks a follow-up question about difficulty preferences, but this time the user chooses not to skip it.

nodes.label: Specify pilot grid difficulty and presentation preferences
nodes.detail: The participant requests one easier and one trickier version of the pilot grid and chooses to display the full shuffled 4×4 grid at once.

nodes.label: Present easier Version A and trickier Version B of the pilot grid
Choose Version B difficulty and finalize the eight-grid format
nodes.detail: The participant selects the trickier Version B style for all grids from Claude's follow-up question.

nodes.label: Ask a follow-up question regarding time allocation
Choose ~3 min per grid
nodes.detail: The participant selects approximately three minutes per grid.

nodes.label: Estimate grid capacity (13-14 at 3 min) and ask how to use the slack
Choose 8 grids in total
nodes.detail: The participant selects eight grids in total, two per topic pairing.

nodes.label: Build the full set of 8 Connections grids
nodes.detail: Gathers any remaining source content via web search and generates the complete 8-grid Connections document covering all topic pairings.

nodes.label: Monitor the full 8-grid generation
nodes.detail: Waits for Claude to finish building the full grid document, then decides the result is fine as is (00:26:51) and moves on to review it.

nodes.label: Review the generated Connections grids and answer explanations
Identify grids needing final trimming
nodes.detail: Reviews the completed 8-grid document and flags the categories left with 5 candidate items instead of the required 4 per grid slot.

nodes.label: Asks three clarifying questions regarding Grid 1 and Grid 8
Choose final items for ambiguous categories
nodes.detail: Answers Claude's clarifying questions, specifying exactly which item to drop from each over-filled category (e.g. dropping 'Increased SSI Risk' from Grid 1's Green category).

nodes.label: Correct grid contents to exactly 4 items per category
nodes.detail: Edits the grid document to enforce clean 4-4-4-4 category counts, catches and redoes an initial edit that left gaps, then rebuilds and visually verifies both corrected grids.

nodes.label: Request a click-to-reveal PowerPoint and specify pilot requirements
nodes.detail: The participant asks Claude to convert the grids into a PowerPoint with independently clickable boxes that reveal their category colors in any order. She then chooses to test one pilot grid before building all eight.

nodes.label: Ask two clarifying questions regarding click behavior and testing scope
Answers clarifying questions regarding click behavior and testing scope
Build animated pilot via hand-edited slide XML
nodes.detail: Determines the pptx-generation skill doesn't support click-triggered animations, so hand-edits the slide's underlying XML to add independent click-triggered fill-color animations to Grid 1's 16 boxes as a pilot.

nodes.label: Preview and test the pilot in PowerPoint
nodes.detail: Opens the pilot file, reviews the static layout, then runs the slideshow to test whether clicking each box reveals its color.

nodes.label: Discover and report the click-order bug
nodes.detail: Finds that boxes only light up correctly when clicked in the order the animations were built, not the order actually clicked, and reports this back to Claude.

nodes.label: Diagnose PowerPoint limitation and propose manual-setup pivot
nodes.detail: Explains that PowerPoint's animation model can't reliably support true any-order click triggers this way, and proposes instead building static, clearly-labeled grids plus a step-by-step guide for her to wire up triggers manually.

nodes.label: Review the limitation and manual-setup pivot, approve the static-grid plus manual-setup plan
nodes.detail: Agrees to the static-grid approach with a how-to guide and prepares to download the files to start the manual work.

nodes.label: Build static 8-grid deck with named boxes and trigger how-to
Briefly take a look at the Grid 1 ERAS PPT
Download and open the static-grid deck
nodes.detail: Downloads the 8-grid static PowerPoint file with descriptively-named boxes (e.g. G1_box_0_0_yellow) and opens it, confirming her second-monitor display is recognized.

nodes.label: Write up a condensed one-page cheat sheet
Begin per-box animation setup for Grid 1
nodes.detail: Starts manually adding a fill-color animation and click-trigger to each of Grid 1's 16 boxes, following Claude's written trigger cheatsheet for the Animations tab/Animation Pane workflow.
nodes.softwares: Microsoft PowerPoint, Markdown file viewer (trigger cheatsheet)

nodes.label: Troubleshoot PowerPoint's animation UI
nodes.detail: Hunts for the Effect Options and Animation Pane controls needed to set each box's trigger, repeatedly losing and re-finding the right panel.

nodes.label: Continue building Grid 1's per-box color-trigger animations
nodes.detail: Works through the remaining boxes' fill-color and trigger settings one at a time, matching each to its category color (yellow/green/blue/purple) and assigning the correct trigger shape.
nodes.softwares: Microsoft PowerPoint, Markdown file viewer (trigger cheatsheet)

nodes.label: Complete and test Grid 1's interactive reveal
nodes.detail: Finishes configuring triggers for all 16 boxes and plays the slideshow to confirm each box now reveals its color correctly in any click order.

user_response.label: modify
user_response.reasoning: a70 is the source because she asks Claude for a PowerPoint where clicking any grid box reveals its color. Claude's first attempt (a73) fails her test, and after the refinement through a76 and a77, a78 is the final output: a static 8-grid deck with named boxes plus a how-to for adding triggers herself. Claude couldn't deliver the exact request, so this is its alternative. She removes the longer title text Claude put on the Grid 1 slide, then follows the how-to to add fill-color animations and triggers to all 16 boxes and confirms in slideshow that it works in any click order. The label is modify because she uses Claude's deck but deletes and modifies some parts of its content.

user_response.label: modify
user_response.reasoning: a70 is the source because she asks Claude for a clickable grid deck. a81 is the target because it is the one-page checklist Claude writes for the manual trigger setup. She follows its steps on all 16 boxes of Grid 1 (select box, Add Animation, Fill Color, Effect Options, Trigger on click of the matching box) and plays the slideshow to confirm it works. She doesn't use the exact hex colors the cheatsheet lists and picks her own shades for each category. The label is modify because she follows Claude's steps but changes the colors.

nodes.label: Confirm Grid 1 success and ask about replication shortcuts
nodes.detail: Confirms Grid 1's interactive reveal works correctly and asks Claude whether PowerPoint has a way to copy all the trigger animations onto the remaining slides instead of rebuilding them by hand.

nodes.label: Recommend Animation Painter with a trigger-targeting caveat
nodes.detail: Explains how to use PowerPoint's Animation Painter to copy each box's fill-color animation and trigger onto the corresponding box on other grids, warning that trigger targeting must be verified after each paint since it can silently stay bound to the wrong shape; also suggests duplicating slides as a possibly faster alternative.

nodes.label: Review the recommendation and replicate Grid 1's animations onto Grid 2
nodes.detail: Skips Claude's follow-up question. Uses Animation Painter box-by-box to copy Grid 1's fill-color/trigger animations onto Grid 2, adjusting each box's target color and label to match Grid 2's content.

user_response.label: adopt
user_response.reasoning: a86 is the source because, after finishing Grid 1, she asks Claude whether PowerPoint can copy the trigger animations onto the other slides. a87 is the target because it recommends Animation Painter, one box at a time, with a warning to verify each trigger target. She uses it box by box on Grid 2, adjusting each box's color and target, says she likes doing it this way, and continues the same way on Grids 3 to 8. The label is adopt because she follows Claude's method as given. She skips its follow-up question and the duplicate-slides alternative.

nodes.label: Repeat the copy-and-adjust process for Grids 3-8
nodes.detail: Continues the same Animation Painter workflow across the remaining six grids, catching and undoing (Ctrl+Z) at least one misapplied animation along the way.

nodes.label: Finish, save, and download the completed deck
nodes.detail: Completes the final grid's animations, saves the presentation, and downloads Obgyn connections grids DOCX.

user_response.label: adopt
user_response.reasoning: a50 is the source because she asks Claude for a pilot Connections grid before the full set. a69 is the target because it is the final corrected 8-grid doc after the pilot, difficulty, grid count and trimming choices. She uses it as the basis for the PowerPoint build and, at the end, downloads the 'connection scripts' to keep as her host reference. The label is adopt because she keeps the grids as Claude finalized them.
